posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
I am trying to shoot silver halide with 514nm and the hologram are coming out violet and dim. Any suggestions to get them at least green without post swelling with something not found around the house? Or any other technique. I remember trying sugar water post swelling with minimal sucess.

VRP-M with JD2 dev and bleach.

Immediate responses welcome. 

Meanwhile I will search the gallery for someone shooting in silver with green and may find something.

Thanks,

John

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Ok, old habbits die hard. I didn't blow dry the last one and it was green. I thought I could blow dry the first one very lightly from far away but I guess not for this emulsion with this wavelength.

Do any of you get a green shift when blow drying silver and shooting in red?

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
Sort of.

The JD2 bleach will cause some shrinkage of the emulsion. Instead, use something like EDTA.

posts.author: Martin
posts.content_md:
> **MichaelH:** Sort of.The JD2 bleach will cause some shrinkage of the emulsion. Instead, use something like EDTA.

Yes, or take a DCG-like approach:

after the final water wash, dehydrate/dry the emulsion in isopropyl alcohol + warm air...

posts.author: Tony
posts.content_md:
I'm sure it's the dichromate bleach causing most of the shrinkage. Try Fe EDTA or CuSO4 bleach. I've never noticed any effect from moderate blow drying in silver. Also, pyro developer (JD2) causes some tanning and may be responsible for some shrinkage.

You could also try a post-swell with TEA or sugar.

Or, preswell with TEA and you've got your UV hologram!

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Thanks all.

Michael, for what I am doing I originally thought I would need to stick to the developer Integraf suggests for VPR-M so it follows their kit suggestions. But now in thinking, most kit purchasers will be using a different film and laser wavelength (red). So I will try the bleach you suggested.

Martin, I will try alcohol. It's not like I don't have plenty of the stuff on hand.

Tony, I suspect the pryo is also responsible. I remember when we used to shoot silver masters to repay with a HeCd, Pyro was the developer of choice.
